name: VA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 6-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Subramanyam's huge fundraising edge ($1.17M vs ~$107K) and cash advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 95-97%
First-term incumbent with no serious outside spending against him
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Subramanyam: a D+6 seat, an incumbent with a ten-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets pricing his win at 95% or higher. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict that picture, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unusually strong midterm-style backlash environment could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 10th District leans Democratic by about six points, and first-term incumbent Suhas Subramanyam is seeking reelection with a commanding financial position. He has raised roughly $1.17 million and holds about $583,000 on hand, while Republican Dave Beckwith has raised about $107,000 with $54,000 available. No outside groups are opposing the incumbent, and modest outside support favors him.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's resources, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at 95 to 97 percent. A minor independent candidate is on the ballot but shows no measurable activity. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being how large the eventual margin turns out rather than who wins.
